dimensions.note: No credential at all: a plain GET with Accept and User-Agent; a CA file is read for verification only. Nothing sensitive exists to record or log.
One info line on entry, one on the outcome with URL, status and latency, a warning with the reason when not ok; structured placeholders throughout.

A URL that is not http or https, or a caFile that cannot be read, fails before anything is recorded; every runtime outcome, a wrong status, a missing body text, a refused connection, a timeout, a chain that does not verify, is a record with ok false and the reason, fetch's wrapped cause included.

10 unit tests against a real local server cover every outcome, redirects followed, capped and refused, the timeout, the cause chain and both checks; HTTP_E2E=1 verifies a public HTTPS site and sees self-signed.badssl.com recorded as tls failed.
Read-only; a run is one GET with a hard timeout; redirects are bounded by maxRedirects; the body is read only when asked.
Plain HTTP semantics: 3xx with Location is a redirect, anything else is the final answer; the status compared is the final one.
Response bodies are cancelled when not read, the CA HttpClient is closed in finally, the timeout timer is cleared and the outer abort listener removed on every path.
README uses example.org and self-signed.badssl.com, the public test host; no real infrastructure named.
One closed z.object record with nullable fields where an answer may be missing.
health: lifetime infinite, garbageCollection 10, so the history is the uptime log.
A probe, not a managed resource.
arguments (policy) and ca-readable (local); health is a read, so they run with swamp model validate.
